Q: Insert a new row only if a row with the same subset of values doesn't exist yet A:

Then define UNIQUE KEY any_name(user_id,second,third) for your wanted unique combination. With this INSERT .. ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE ... works fine.

Q: Numeric or value error: character string buffer too small ORA-06512 A:

You code does not use VARCHAR2 data types so there are no character strings in the code that you have shown us.

The only hint of code that you have not shown us is the bind variables :v_items and :v_amount. You need to make sure that those two bind variables can receive sufficient characters to the total number of items and the total cost of all those items. (Or better, make sure that they are numeric bind variables and not strings).

For example, if your final code was:

DECLARE
  total_quantity VARCHAR2(4);
  total_amount   VARCHAR2(4);
BEGIN
  EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'BEGIN get_order_summary(499, :v_items, :v_amount); END;'
    USING OUT total_quantity, OUT total_amount;

  DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE(total_quantity || ', ' || total_amount);
END;
/

Then the output is:

ORA-06502: PL/SQL: numeric or value error: character string buffer too small
ORA-06512: at line 1
ORA-06512: at line 5

As 4 characters is too small to store the total amount.

Changing the code to:

DECLARE
  total_quantity VARCHAR2(10);
  total_amount   VARCHAR2(30);
BEGIN
  EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'BEGIN get_order_summary(499, :v_items, :v_amount); END;'
    USING OUT total_quantity, OUT total_amount;

  DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE(total_quantity || ', ' || total_amount);
END;
/

Works and outputs 5, 83.35.

fiddle

You need to ensure that whatever front-end you are using to access the database is provisioning a large enough string buffer to accept your data - but that is code that you have not shared with us so we cannot comment on it.

You can use your data to make assumptions about the size of the values:

  • If each order has 100 line items.
  • If maximum quantity per line item is 1,000.
  • If the unit price is NUMBER(10,2) then the maximum unit price is 99999999.99.

Then given those assumptions:

  • The maximum total quantity is 100 * 1000 = 100,000.
  • The maximum total amount is 100 * 1000 * 99999999.99 which is 9,999,999,999,000.00

So, assuming that those assumptions are accurate then you need a 5-character string for the total quantity and an 16-character string (13 integer digits, 1 decimal place and 2 decimal digits) for the total amount.

However, they probably are not accurate estimates as you may have more line items and the other values may be under-estimates, so you will want to significantly increase the size of your strings so that as your application grows it can handle the data.

Q: Python algorithm to automatically propagate inequalities transitively A:

Note that

if ineq == (m, n):
    assert False, f"Inequality {m} < {n} already exists in the registry."

can be replaced by

assert ineq != (m, n), f"Inequality {m} < {n} already exists in the registry."

More importantly, self.inequalities should be a set, not a list. use { ... } instead of [ ... ] to create a set instead of a list. Then, instead of

for ineq in self.inequalities:
    if ineq == (m, n):
        ...

you can write directly

if (m, n) in self.inequalities:
    ...

Q: Laravel 12 Cors - not working for me, what am I missing? A:

Map allowed_origins like this

    'http://localhost:3000',
    'http://127.0.0.1:3000',

Q: Why is altool extremely slow or stuck when uploading an IPA to Apple? A:

First of all Apple does not actively improve altool anymore.

Recommended Solutions

Stop Using altool. Use one of these instead:

Xcode Organizer (Most Reliable)

Archive → Distribute → App Store Connect

Fastest and most stable.

Transporter App

Use Transporter by downloading from Mac App Store. It uses the same backend but:

  • Better progress reporting

  • Better retry handling

  • Doesn’t hang like altool

Best CLI alternative:

xcrun iTMSTransporter

App Store Connect API + Fastlane

If you automate, use Fastlanewith:

fastlane pilot upload

More reliable than raw altool.

altool is legacy and unreliable in 2025+.

Q: Find character from position in Delphi A:

You can only do this if the particular control in question (listbox in this case) provides such a function. There's no generic way this can be done as controls are free to use varying horizontal and vertical layout based on the selected font, and so on.
